specification:
Type: microsim **sim-id:** training-evaluation-matcher
**Library:** p5.js
**Status:** Specified
**Bloom Level:** Understand
**Bloom Verb:** classify
**Learning Objective:** The learner will classify each of eight pieces of evidence under Reaction, Learning, Behavior, or Results, with at least 7 of 8 correct on the first attempt. **Prerequisites:** Exit Survey, Training Evaluation (both defined in this chapter above this block). **Evidence of Mastery:** For each item the learner commits one of four levels. A placement is correct when it matches the Correct level column in Content. Mastery is at least 7 of 8 correct on the first attempt. Reading the four levels is exploration, not evidence. **Misconceptions:** (1) An exit survey shows that the training worked. (2) A certificate count shows changed behavior. (3) Reuse by others is a measure of satisfaction. **Instructional Rationale:** Classifying evidence by level is an Understand-level action that shows how far each piece of evidence reaches. Two items per level teach the learner to see what an exit survey cannot show. **Content:** The four levels and their meanings: Reaction (how participants felt about the training), Learning (what they learned), Behavior (what they do differently afterward), Results (what changed because of it). The eight items (all made up): | # | Evidence | Correct level | Why (shown as feedback) | |---|---|---|---| | 1 | 18 of 19 respondents rated the day 4 or 5. | Reaction | It records how participants felt. | | 2 | Participants wrote that the pace was too fast. | Reaction | It is an opinion about the training. | | 3 | Teachers' calibration scores differed from the consensus by 1.1 points on average. | Learning | It measures a skill gained. | | 4 | 17 of 20 teachers earned the certificate. | Learning | It shows the skills were demonstrated. | | 5 | 12 of 17 certified teachers scored another resource within three months. | Behavior | It shows use of the skill afterward. | | 6 | Teachers kept a findings log on their own reviews. | Behavior | It shows a practice carried over. | | 7 | 20 improved components were published. | Results | They are products of the training. | | 8 | 9 components were reused by another teacher within three months. | Results | Reuse is an outcome beyond the participants. | **Provenance:** The items are illustrative examples written for this chapter, and the sim labels them "illustrative examples". The four levels follow the model of Donald Kirkpatrick, as described in the chapter section "Training Evaluation". **Rules:** Each item has exactly one correct level, two per level. **Learner Activity:** 1. The learner sees one item and the four levels. 2. The learner places the item under a level, and the placement is committed. 3. The sim shows whether it was correct and the Why text. 4. After item 8 the sim shows the summary. **Feedback:** 8 items in a shuffled order, one attempt each. Correct: "Correct: [level]. [Why]". Incorrect: "Not quite. This is [level]. [Why]". The summary shows "[n] of 8 correct on the first attempt". At 7 or more it adds "You can place evidence at the right level." Below 7 it lists the Why text of each missed item. **Starting State:** The first item in the shuffled order and the four levels. The question shown is "What does this evidence show?" **Chapter Anchors:** The chapter's table of four levels gives two examples of evidence for each level.
